title: Malfunctions
subtitle: Misfire, hang fire, squib load, stove-pipe jam, failure to go into battery

lines: In this episode: five malfunctions, what causes them, and the corrective action for each.
The aim is for you to safely and confidently operate firearms in different circumstances.

scenes.heading: Five terms to explain
lines: You must be able to explain five terms, starting with a misfire.
Then a hang fire.
A squib load.
A stove-pipe jam.
And a failure to go into battery.

scenes.definition: A failure of the cartridge to fire after the primer has been struck.
lines: A misfire is a failure of the cartridge to fire after the primer has been struck.
This is caused by a faulty or dead primer.
It can also be caused by a light strike, or soft strike, by the firing pin on the primer.

scenes.heading: Misfire: corrective action
bullets: Revolver: simply squeeze the trigger again

lines.text: For a semi-automatic pistol, the corrective action is the Immediate Action Drill: Tap, Rack, Assess.
For a revolver, simply squeeze the trigger again.

lines: That will cause the cylinder to turn, and line up a new round with the barrel.
We'll practise Tap, Rack, Assess in the next episode.

scenes.definition: A perceptible delay in the ignition of the cartridge after the primer has been struck.
lines: A hang fire is a perceptible delay in the ignition of the cartridge after the primer has been struck.
A hang fire can take up to five seconds to ignite.
Hang fires are not very common in modern day ammunition.

rule.label: Corrective action
rule.text: Hang fire: wait five seconds before reloading.

lines: The corrective action is to wait five seconds before reloading.
However, if you are faced with a life threatening situation, you will treat a hang fire as a misfire.
The book puts the chances of you experiencing a hang fire in your lifetime at about ten million to one.

scenes.definition: A cartridge that develops less than normal pressure when fired.
lines: A squib load can be defined as a cartridge that develops less than normal pressure when fired.
This is usually due to powder contamination, or not enough powder in the case.
It is unlikely that the bullet will exit the muzzle.

scenes.heading: Recognising a squib load
bullets: Very little sound: a low, dull pop

lines.text: A squib load is easily identifiable, as it has almost no recoil.
And there will be very little sound produced at the time of firing.

lines: Instead of a loud bang and the normal recoil, all you will hear is a low, dull pop, with very little recoil felt.

rule.label: Corrective action
rule.text: Squib load: take your firearm to a gunsmith.

lines: The corrective action: take your firearm to a gunsmith.
The bullet will have to be physically removed from the barrel by a qualified gunsmith before firing the next shot.
If this is not done, you can not only damage the firearm, but could also suffer severe injuries to yourself.

lines.text: The stove-pipe jam is caused when the empty case fails to eject completely from the firearm.
The corrective action: bring the firearm closer to your body, making sure your finger is off the trigger.
Take your non-gun hand, and sweep it back towards you over the ejection port, sweeping the case out of the port.
Muzzle control is important during this malfunction drill.
When the slide fails to go into battery, the slide has not moved all the way forward.
It has therefore not properly chambered the cartridge.
The corrective action is Tap, Rack, Assess.

scenes.question: What is a hang fire?
options: A cartridge with less than normal pressure
An empty case stuck in the ejection port
lines: What is a hang fire?
Pause the video if you need a moment.
reveal: A perceptible delay in the ignition of the cartridge after the primer has been struck.
It can take up to five seconds to ignite, so wait five seconds before reloading.

scenes.question: A shot gives a low, dull pop and very little recoil. What do you do?
options: Take the firearm to a gunsmith
lines: You fire a shot, and hear only a low, dull pop, with very little recoil.
What do you do?
reveal: Take your firearm to a gunsmith.
It's a squib load, and the bullet must be removed from the barrel by a qualified gunsmith before the next shot.

points: Misfire: Tap, Rack, Assess; revolver: trigger again
Squib load: take it to a gunsmith
Stove-pipe: sweep the case out of the port
Failure to go into battery: Tap, Rack, Assess
lines: So, for a misfire, Tap, Rack, Assess on a pistol, or squeeze the trigger again on a revolver.
For a hang fire, wait five seconds before reloading.
For a squib load, take your firearm to a gunsmith.
For a stove-pipe jam, sweep the case out of the ejection port.
And for a failure to go into battery, Tap, Rack, Assess.
